captions.text: A ball and a feather start falling at the same time. The ball lands first, the feather floats slowly down.

scenes.title: Is it because of the weight? No. The feather offers the air a lot o…

captions.text: Is it because of the weight? No. The feather offers the air a lot of surface, and the air slows it down a lot. It hardly slows the ball.
A short pause to think: Why does the feather land later than the ball?

scenes.title: Now we pump the air out of a tube. In a vacuum, the ball and the fe…

captions.text: Now we pump the air out of a tube. In a vacuum, the ball and the feather fall exactly equally fast.
A short pause to think: What happens to the ball and the feather without air?

scenes.title: Without air, all bodies fall equally fast, however heavy they are. …

captions.text: Without air, all bodies fall equally fast, however heavy they are. Differences in everyday life come from the air.
